decisions.reason: As a flagship launch shown on the home page and tied to the firm's announced move toward innovative multichannel cloud communications, management is likely to continue backing it because investment and public commitment are high and any weaker uptake can still be framed as temporary.
This service builds directly on the core offer, had its own page, and even showed a customer reference, so sunk development effort and visible market validation make continued commitment likely.

Although less prominently presented, it still extends the firm's established messaging portfolio and serves regulated multichannel workflows, so management would tend to retain it unless results became clearly and persistently weak.

Because this optimization feature is very close to the core fax business and likely inexpensive to maintain once developed, the firm has reasons to keep it as part of its portfolio rather than concede a failed launch.

Security is central to the firm's value proposition and future direction, so despite modest visibility the firm is likely to persist with this offering given prior R&D investment and the ability to attribute slow traction to customer adoption timing.
